Hon'ble Suresh Kumar Gupta,J.
Vakalatnama filed by Mr. Digvijay Singh, Advocate on behalf of the opposite party no.2 is taken on
record.

Heard learned counsel for applicant/petitioner, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the
material available on record.

The present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed with the prayer to quash the impugned charge sheet dated 10.1.2021 as well as cognizance/summoning order dated 19.3.2021 and further quash entire proceedings of Case No. 14178 of 2021 arising out of Case Crime/FIR no.
73 of 2020, under Sections 498A,504,506 I.P.C., Police Station- Mahila Thana, District- Lucknow.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At the very outset, learned counsel for applicant has submitted that the applicant is the husband of the opposite party no.2.

The dispute between the parties has been amicably settled and the parties have entered into a compromise by means of compromise deed, which has been duly verified by the court concerned on 7.1.2023 (Annexure-7 to this petition).
Learned counsel for opposite party no. 2 does not dispute the correctness of the submission made by learned counsel for petitioner or the correctness of the documents relied upon by him.
He submits that opposite party no. 2 has no objection, if the proceedings in the aforesaid are quashed.

From perusal of the record, it is apparent that the parties have entered into compromise and have settled their dispute amicably and it is highly doubtful if the ingredients of the offence as alleged are made out.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties regarding the compromise entered into between the parties and taking all these factors into consideration cumulatively, the compromise between the parties be accepted

and further taking into account the legal position as laid down by the Apex Court in the cases of B.S.
Joshi Vs. State of Haryana; 2003 (4) SCC 675 as well as State of Madhya Pradesh vs Laxmi Narayan and others; AIR 2019 SC 1296, the entire proceedings of the aforesaid case is hereby quashed.
